title: plugin-voice: no audio wake-word detector
body:
**Area**: Voice / Wake word
**Severity**: medium (missing capability)
**Parity id**: OC-101 (ledger: open)

## Description

OpenClaw 2026.11.3: gateway-wide wake words synced across nodes; Swabble on macOS (source `src/infra/voicewake.ts:27`, Observed).
Measured on OpenClaw: verdict `not-exercised`. needs the macOS app with a microphone (Reported).

theoclaw 0.1.0: verdict `absent`. stripWakeWord lives in the unwired talk-session module; no variable configures a wake word (Observed).

Both were measured side by side on 2026-11-10.

## Evidence

- Observed: `theoclaw@0.1.0` dist/voice/talk-session.js:3 stripWakeWord works on text transcripts only
- Observed: no audio wake-word detector in `@theokit/plugin-voice@0.11.2` or elsewhere in TheoKit (grep wake: only TalkOptions UI)

## What to build

An on-device keyword-spotting detector in `@theokit/plugin-voice` that listens to the microphone stream and emits an event when the configured wake word is heard, without sending audio to a provider before it fires. TheoClaw's `stripWakeWord` (`dist/voice/talk-session.js:3`) only works on text transcripts.

## Acceptance

With the wake word 'theo' configured in the browser helper, saying 'theo' fires the wake event and starts a recording; speech without the word fires nothing and sends no STT request.

How this is checked, so it runs without a person at a microphone: an end-to-end test drives the browser helper in headless Chromium with recorded speech as the microphone (`--use-fake-device-for-media-stream --use-file-for-fake-audio-capture=<wav>`). Commit the recordings as fixtures: a few utterances of "theo" for enrollment, one more "theo" that must fire the wake event and start a recording, and a sentence without the word that must fire nothing and send no STT request (assert on the network log). The recordings may come from a speech synthesizer as long as they are real audio files, not synthetic tones.

A unit test with synthetic tones or a stubbed recorder does not satisfy this issue on its own.

title: sandbox: no E2B backend ships, though the docs name it; aifactory had to write one
body:
**Area:** sandbox
**Severity:** medium (every consumer that wants a cloud sandbox writes its own adapter)
**Build under test:** @theokit/agents 16.3.x on @theokit/sdk 5.x

## Description

`sandbox/types.d.ts` says remote backends (Docker, Firecracker, E2B) only implement `execute` and `uploadFile`, and `provision.d.ts` says `provisionRepo` runs on Local/Docker/E2B, but no E2B backend ships. aifactory needed one on 2026-11-11 and wrote it outside the SDK: `src/server/factory/e2b-sandbox.ts` in paulohenriquevn/aifactory (commit 8d29e52).

What the adapter had to solve, each one verified against E2B with a real sandbox (`e2b-sandbox.e2e.test.ts`, 7 tests passing):

1. **Exit codes.** `sandbox.commands.run` throws `CommandExitError` for a non-zero exit and `TimeoutError` for a timeout. A backend has to turn the first into `{ exitCode }` and the second into 124.
2. **A dead sandbox is not a timeout.** `SandboxNotRunningError` and `SandboxUnreachableError` extend `TimeoutError`; mapping every `TimeoutError` to 124 reports a stopped sandbox as a slow command, and the caller keeps going.
3. **Dockerfile `ENV` is not applied.** A template built with `Template().fromDockerfile(...)` starts without the Dockerfile's `ENV` lines, so `HOME`, `CI` and friends must be passed in `envs` at creation.
4. **Node does not trust E2B's egress proxy.** With `network.rules[].transform.headers` (credentials attached outside the sandbox), curl and git work but `fetch` fails with `unable to verify the first certificate` until `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt`.
5. **Egress.** `allowOut` plus `denyOut: [ALL_TRAFFIC]` gives the allowlist; `updateNetwork` replaces the whole policy, so a credential renewal must resend the deny and every rule.
6. **Snapshots.** `Sandbox.deleteSnapshot` fails with `400: cannot delete template ... because there are running sandboxes using it` while a sandbox restored from it runs, so the deletion has to wait for that sandbox to stop.

## Proposal

An `E2BSandbox extends SandboxBackend` in `@theokit/sdk/sandbox` (with `e2b` as an optional peer) covering 1 to 4, and the `networkPolicy` it was created with, so `SandboxNetworkPolicy` (#1130 in usetheokit/theokit) describes it. Credential headers, renewal and snapshots could follow the same shape, since every VM backend needs them (the Vercel one in aifactory does the same three things).

## Related

- usetheokit/theokit#1130 (declarative `networkPolicy` and `dispose`, closed)
- paulohenriquevn/aifactory#26

title: gateway-wecom, gateway-wechat: five critical Sonar findings in the signature and crypto code drop security and reliability to D
body:
## Description

The required check "SonarCloud Code Analysis" fails on `workspace`, which blocks the `workspace -> develop` pull request #327. Two of its three failed conditions are "D Security Rating on New Code" and "D Reliability Rating on New Code". Five critical findings in the new WeChat and WeCom crypto files cause both. This issue covers those two conditions; duplication is a separate issue.

## Repro

- Check run: https://sonarcloud.io/dashboard?id=usetheokit_theokit-gateways&pullRequest=327 (GitHub check run 130477338026 on 00af16f, 5 annotations)
- Command: `gh api repos/usetheokit/theokit-gateways/check-runs/130477338026/annotations`

```
packages/gateway-wecom/src/crypto.ts:18   S4790 VULNERABILITY  Make sure this weak hash algorithm is not used in a sensitive context here.
packages/gateway-wecom/src/crypto.ts:20   S2871 BUG            Provide a compare function that depends on "String.localeCompare", to reliably sort elements alphabetically.
packages/gateway-wecom/src/crypto.ts:76   S5542 VULNERABILITY  Use a secure mode and padding scheme.
packages/gateway-wechat/src/signature.ts:10  S4790 VULNERABILITY  Make sure this weak hash algorithm is not used in a sensitive context here.
packages/gateway-wechat/src/signature.ts:12  S2871 BUG            Provide a compare function that depends on "String.localeCompare", to reliably sort elements alphabetically.
```

All five are severity CRITICAL in the SonarCloud issues API.

## Expected

Security and reliability ratings on new code at A.

## Actual

Both at D.

## Probable cause

- `packages/gateway-wechat/src/signature.ts:10-12` (3efe7e7, #345) and `packages/gateway-wecom/src/crypto.ts:18-20` (5980e00, #349) compute `sha1([...].sort().join(""))`.
- `packages/gateway-wecom/src/crypto.ts:76` (5980e00) uses `aes-256-cbc` with the IV taken from the key and manual PKCS#7 padding.

SHA-1 signatures, AES-256-CBC, the key-derived IV and the 32-byte PKCS#7 block are what the WeChat and WeCom callback protocols require (the file headers state the formulas). The adapters cannot pick another algorithm and still talk to the platform. What is fixable:

1. S2871 (the two BUGs): `.sort()` on strings without a comparator. The WeChat/WeCom spec sorts by byte order, so the comparator should be an explicit code-unit comparison (`(a, b) => (a < b ? -1 : a > b ? 1 : 0)`), not `localeCompare`, which would change the signature for mixed-case input. Add a test with mixed-case token and nonce that pins the expected signature.
2. S4790 and S5542 (the three VULNERABILITYs): mark them as accepted in code with a `// NOSONAR` comment on the line that names the protocol requirement, or have the repository owner resolve them as "Accepted" in SonarCloud. Check how earlier gateways that verify SHA-1 or CBC signatures were handled and do the same.

## Acceptance

- The SonarCloud quality gate on the `workspace -> develop` pull request no longer lists "Reliability Rating on New Code" or "Security Rating on New Code" as failed conditions.
- A test in `gateway-wechat` and one in `gateway-wecom` sign a request whose token and nonce mix upper and lower case and match a signature computed by the platform's documented algorithm.
- The "SonarCloud Code Analysis" check passes on `workspace` once this and the separate duplication issue are both fixed.

title: ci: Playwright 1.60.0 cannot install Chromium on the ubuntu-26.04 runner, failing Browser + stories
body:
## Description

The `Browser + stories` job fails before running a single test, which makes the CI workflow red and blocks the `workspace -> develop` pull request #174. GitHub's `ubuntu-latest` runner now resolves to Ubuntu 26.04, and the pinned Playwright 1.60.0 refuses to install Chromium there. No code change caused it; a re-run fails the same way.

## Repro

- Run: https://github.com/usetheokit/theokit-ui/actions/runs/42994057404 (attempt 2, job `Browser + stories`, step `Install Playwright Chromium`)
- Command (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:116-118`, working directory `packages/ui`): `pnpm exec playwright install --with-deps chromium`

```
Runner Image
Image: ubuntu-26.04
Version: 20261101.186.1

BEWARE: your OS is not officially supported by Playwright; installing dependencies for ubuntu26.04-x64 as a fallback.
Cannot install dependencies for ubuntu26.04-x64 with Playwright 1.60.0!
Failed to install browsers
Error: ERROR: Playwright does not support chromium on ubuntu26.04-x64
##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.
```

## Expected

Chromium installs and the job goes on to `quality:a11y`, `quality:visual` and `ladle:build`, as in the last green `develop` run 36186072037, which ran on `Image: ubuntu-24.04`.

## Actual

The install step exits 1 on attempt 1 and attempt 2.

## Probable cause

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml:103` runs the job on `ubuntu-latest`, which moved from `ubuntu-24.04` to `ubuntu-26.04`.
- `packages/ui/package.json:574` declares `"@playwright/test": "^1.60.0"` and `pnpm-lock.yaml` resolves `playwright@1.60.0`, which has no host entry for Ubuntu 26.04.
- The latest release, `playwright-core@1.65.0`, lists `ubuntu26.04-x64` in its host table (checked in the published package). It has not been run in this repository's CI.

Two fixes, either one sufficient:

1. Bump `@playwright/test` to a release that supports Ubuntu 26.04 (1.65.0 or later) and refresh the lockfile. Visual snapshots may change with the new Chromium, so `quality:visual` has to pass, and any baseline update must be reviewed rather than accepted blindly.
2. Pin the job to `runs-on: ubuntu-24.04` until the upgrade lands. This is quicker, and it keeps the visual baselines tied to the image they were taken on.

## Acceptance

- The `Browser + stories` job of the CI workflow passes on `workspace`, including `Install Playwright Chromium`, `quality:a11y`, `quality:visual` and `ladle:build`.

title: gateway-email: the first connect dispatches the whole unread backlog, from inside start()
body:
**Area:** gateway-email
**Severity:** high (on a real mailbox the first start dispatches years of unread mail; under an open policy the host answers all of it)
**Build under test:** `@theokit/gateway-email` 0.3.1 (through theoclaw 0.1.0); the same code is in the published 0.4.0 (`_drainUnseen` in `dist/index.js`)
**Environment:** a Gmail IMAP mailbox with 22,421 messages, 22,353 of them unseen

## Description
On its first connect the adapter fetches every UNSEEN message and dispatches each one to the handler, and it does so before `start()` resolves. A host that bounds its start time gives up on the channel while the adapter keeps dispatching.

## Repro
1. Start theoclaw with only e-mail configured and `THEOCLAW_DM_POLICY=open` on a mailbox with a large unseen backlog.
2. After 30 s theoclaw prints `email: start timed out after 30000 ms`.
3. In the next two minutes the adapter logs 20,662 `[email] dropped automated sender: ...` lines while walking the backlog. I stopped it before it reached human mail, which the open policy would have answered.

Reproduced 1/1 on 2026-11-10.

## Expected
A first connect sets a baseline (the mailbox's current UIDNEXT, with its UIDVALIDITY) and dispatches only mail that arrives after it, as OpenClaw's imap plugin does (`cursor=baseline uidValidity=1761846127 uid=26316`, existing mail not dispatched). Backlog processing, if wanted, is an explicit option with a cap. `start()` resolves once the connection and the baseline are set, not after a drain.

## Actual
Every unseen message is dispatched on first connect, from inside `start()`.

## Probable cause
`_drainUnseen()` calls `fetchUnseen()` and dispatches all results, and the start path awaits it. theokit-gateways#11 fixed re-delivery on reconnect by marking `\Seen`; it did not add a starting point, and mail the adapter drops (automated senders) is still in the backlog the next time.

## Suggested fix
Persist a per-mailbox cursor `{uidValidity, uid}` through the adapter's state seam; on first connect without one, take UIDNEXT as the baseline and dispatch nothing older. Reset the cursor when UIDVALIDITY changes. Resolve `start()` before any dispatch. Tests with a fake IMAP client: first connect with 3 unseen dispatches 0; a new message after it dispatches 1; a restart dispatches nothing already past the cursor.

## Related
- usetheokit/theokit-gateways#11 (re-delivery on reconnect, closed)

title: llm: nothing bounds the wait for a response's headers, so a request whose response never starts holds the turn for up to 300 s
body:
**Area:** LLM transport (`internal/llm/sse.ts`, `internal/runtime-fetch.ts`)
**Severity:** high. A model request whose response never starts holds the turn for up to 300 s with nothing on screen and nothing in the logs; in TheoClaw it makes H-1 fail (usetheokit/theokit#1497).
**Build under test:** @theokit/sdk 5.15.1 and main at b3998216, Node 22.23.3 (bundled undici 6.28.1), OpenRouter, google/gemini-2.5-flash

## Description
The SDK bounds the time between SSE body reads (`readWithIdleTimeout`, `DEFAULT_SSE_IDLE_MS = 60_000`, `stream_idle_timeout`), but nothing bounds the wait for the response headers. `boundFetch` uses `globalThis.fetch` with no dispatcher, so that wait falls to undici's default `headersTimeout`, which undici documents as 300 s (*Reported*, not measured here). Until then the request neither fails nor retries, so `retrying-client` never gets a chance.

## Evidence (*Observed*, a TheoClaw instance running H-1, traced with `diagnostics_channel` and `ss`)
- Request #1 of the session (a short reply): `sendHeaders`, `bodySent`, `headers 200` about 1 s later.
- The stalled request: `create`, `sendHeaders`, `bodySent`, then no `headers` and no `error` for 90 s, until the test gave up.
- During the stall the process has **no TCP socket to openrouter.ai** at all (`ss -tanp`), its main thread is idle in `ep_poll`, and the CPU profile is 93 of 94 s idle. The request is still pending in the SDK's turn.
- The same prompt sent to OpenRouter directly gets its first content chunk in 0.9 to 1.2 s (6 of 6), and the stall is intermittent (about 1 in 4 H-1 runs locally on develop).

Why the connection disappeared without an error reaching the request is not established; that part may be an undici or a server-side behaviour. Either way the client has no bound on it.

## Expected
A request whose response headers do not arrive within a bound fails with a typed, retryable error (for example `NetworkError` with `code: "response_headers_timeout"`), and the existing retry policy retries it. Suggested shape (not validated): a `fetch` wrapper that races the `fetch` promise against an `AbortSignal.timeout`-style timer combined with the caller's signal, default about 30 s (OpenRouter answers the headers of a streaming request in about 1 s here), configurable next to the SSE idle bound, and `<= 0` disables it like the idle bound does.

A unit test with a fetch that never resolves should see the typed error after the bound and one retry; it fails today because the request waits forever.

## Related
usetheokit/theokit#1497 (H-1 in TheoClaw), usetheokit/theokit#1235.

title: packaging: dist imports 'readline/promises' without the node: scheme, so esbuild bundles fail to resolve it
body:
**Area:** packaging (tsup output)
**Severity:** high. Any consumer that bundles the SDK with esbuild fails to build; TheoCode's `build` fails on the theokit promotion (usetheokit/theokit#1441).
**Build under test:** `@theokit/sdk` 5.15.1 from npm (5.14.0 and 5.15.0 ship the same import)

## Description

`src/internal/mcp/oauth.ts` imports `node:readline/promises`, and the published `dist` imports `'readline/promises'`, without the `node:` scheme (`dist/chunk-X7CE7Y5W.js:11` and `dist/chunk-XOU3CL7S.cjs` in 5.15.1). esbuild 0.28.2 with `platform: 'node'` does not treat the bare `readline/promises` as a builtin, so a bundle that reaches that chunk fails:

```
✘ [ERROR] Could not resolve "readline/promises"
  node_modules/@theokit/sdk/dist/chunk-X7CE7Y5W.js:11:32
```

`fs/promises`, the other subpath builtin in `dist`, resolves, so this one import is the only one that breaks.

## Repro

1. In usetheokit/theokit at `dee33374` (SDK floor 5.15.1): `cd apps/theocode && node tools/build-cli.mjs`
2. The build fails with the error above. Reproduced 2/2 locally and in CI (run 42774785431, job `dep-check / suite at the bottom of every declared range`).

## Expected

`dist` keeps the scheme the source wrote (`node:readline/promises`), so bundlers resolve it as a builtin. tsup strips `node:` by default (`removeNodeProtocol`); setting it to `false` in `packages/sdk/tsup.config.ts` should keep the scheme for every builtin. That is a guess I have not tried.

A test that fails on the bug: scan `dist/**/*.{js,cjs}` after the build and fail on any bare import of a Node builtin subpath (`readline/promises`, `stream/promises`, ...).

## Workaround

title: llm: the streaming path emits Gemini's <ctrl42>call text as text_delta before the calls are recovered
body:
When Gemini writes its tool calls as text (`<ctrl42>call\nprint(default_api.<tool>(...))`, the form #939 recovers), the streaming path sends that text to the consumer as `text_delta` events before the calls are recovered, so the code shows in the visible answer even though the calls run.

Split out of #939 on 2026-11-10: two factory runs of #939 ended at the sandbox's 50-minute limit on this part, and the review of each asked for it.

## What happens

`streamToolCallBufferState` and `StreamSuppressionBuffer` in `packages/sdk/src/internal/llm/hermes-tool-extract.ts` hold back only text that starts with the `<function=` marker. A `<ctrl42>call` stream is never held: run through the accumulator with an allowlist of `computer`, it emits the `text_delta` `<ctrl42>call\nprint(default_api.computer(...))`, while `finish()` recovers the calls (review of the #939 run, round 2).

## Done when

- a streamed response holding the #939 text for a declared tool emits no `text_delta` carrying `<ctrl42>call` or `default_api.`, and the calls still run, shown by an offline test that runs the accumulator with a request-scoped allowlist
- the same stream for a tool the agent did not declare emits the text unchanged
- a stream that starts like the marker and turns out to be plain text is emitted in full, in order

```
+   "tools: createSearxngWebSearchAdapter",

+   "tools: createTavilyWebSearchAdapter",

AssertionError: the layer surface changed. If that was intentional, rewrite the snapshot IN THE SAME commit:
+   "tools: NEW createSearxngWebSearchAdapter",
+   "tools: NEW CreateSearxngWebSearchAdapterOptions",
+   "tools: NEW createTavilyWebSearchAdapter",
+   "tools: NEW CreateTavilyWebSearchAdapterOptions",
```

## Actual

The layer exports four symbols that the declared source of the `tools` subpath (`@theokit/sdk-tools`, root entry) does not export, and the snapshot was not regenerated.

bc007197 (#1603, for #1531) added a re-export at `packages/agents/src/tools-entry.ts:86-94`:

`.github/workflows/ci.yml:928` declares the `sonar` job with `needs: test`. title: theoclaw: duck, pako and qrcode-terminal fail the production licence gate
body:
## Description

The production-tree licence gate fails because two dependencies added to `apps/theoclaw` pull in three packages whose licence strings are not on the allowlist.

## Repro

- Run: https://github.com/usetheokit/theokit/actions/runs/43012060894 (job "License compliance (production tree)", head daa0024). Same on head 24b4d70, run https://github.com/usetheokit/theokit/actions/runs/43014422878.
- Command: `pnpm check:licenses` (runs `node scripts/check-licenses.mjs`)
- Output:

```
✗ 3 production package(s) with an unacceptable licence:
    duck: BSD — not on the allowlist
    pako: (MIT AND Zlib) — not on the allowlist
    qrcode-terminal: Apache 2.0 — not on the allowlist
```

## Expected

Every package in the production tree has a licence string that `scripts/check-licenses.mjs` accepts, either through `ALLOWED` or through an `ALLOWED_WITH_REASON` entry that states the obligation.

## Actual

Three packages are refused and the step exits 1.

## Probable cause

Two merged commits, both from the factory:

- c39b8a9b (#1605, for #1534) added `"mammoth": "^1.13.0"` to `apps/theoclaw/package.json:75`. The lockfile diff of that commit adds `mammoth@1.13.0 -> lop@0.4.2 -> duck@0.1.12` (licence field `BSD`) and `mammoth -> jszip@3.10.2 -> pako@1.0.11` (licence field `(MIT AND Zlib)`).
- e74537ff (#1593, for #1520) added `"qrcode-terminal": "0.12.0"` at `apps/theoclaw/package.json:78`. Its licence field is `Apache 2.0`, which is not the SPDX id `Apache-2.0`.

Not verified: the actual licence texts of `duck` and `qrcode-terminal`. `BSD` without a clause count is ambiguous, so it needs a look at the tarball before it goes on any list. The script's own hint applies: verify the terms, then add the exact string to `ALLOWED` or `ALLOWED_WITH_REASON` with the obligation written down, or drop the dependency.

## Acceptance

- The "License compliance (production tree)" step passes on `workspace`.
- Each of the three strings is either accepted by an entry whose comment names the package and the terms checked, or no longer present in the production tree.

title: hooks: The postRun hook that the 5.12.0 changelog says still fires on a failed run cannot be registered by a consumer: hooks.json skips 'postRun' as not fired
body:
Found by the loop-surface-closure audit of the S-004 release range (`@theokit/sdk@5.11.1` to `@theokit/sdk@5.12.1`, revision `9e337031`), finding `F-fc7517a4`, severity low.

- **Category / persona:** documentation · none
- **Confidence:** confirmed · **Status:** new
- **Steps:** 1. Create .theokit/hooks.json in local.cwd with {hooks:{postRun:[{hooks:[{type:'command',command:'echo fired >> marker'}]}]}} and settingSources ['project']. 2. Agent.create({throwOnError:true}) against a provider answering 401; await run.wait() (rejects). 3. Count marker lines.
- **Expected:** The changelog sentence 'the postRun hook still fires on a failed run' is observable by a consumer: a configured postRun hook runs once
- **Observed:** stderr: `[theokit-sdk] hooks: event "postRun" is not fired by the SDK runtime (supported: PreToolUse, PostToolUse, UserPromptSubmit, Stop) — skipping`; marker has 0 lines. The nearest public event, Stop, also fires 0 times on a failed run (it fires once on a finished run), in 5.12.1 and in 5.11.1 alike.
- **Impact:** A consumer reading the changelog or the public HookEvent type ('The five lifecycle events the runtime actually fires', including postRun) expects a run-end hook on failures and has no way to register one; the repo's own test only observes postRun through an internal spy. No consumer-visible run-end hook fires on a failed run.
- **Suspected cause (hypothesis):** postRun is fired by post-run-lifecycle.ts to the internal hook runner but CLAUDE_CODE_EVENT_MAP has no entry for it and the loader rejects the raw name
- **Retest criterion:** Either a consumer-registrable hook fires once on a failed run (postRun or Stop), or the changelog/HookEvent doc states postRun is internal-only
